title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
note: Fetched. Abstract page: v1 submitted 8 Oct 2026, eight authors, cs.LG; the paper itself is under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Headline: a pretrained multivariate model trained on episodes with target, past-only and known-future covariate roles, reported first on FEV and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval among recent foundation models. The page links no code or weights.

title: Timer-M1 (full text, v1)
note: Fetched. Model: about 121M parameters, 12 layers, patch length 16, quantile head; each layer does temporal attention, feed-forward, then variate attention scaled by a learned per-layer gate. Past-only covariates are masked after the forecast origin, known-future ones stay visible. The text names no code repository, weights location, licence or release date.

title: Timer-M1 (full text, v1)
note: Fetched. Benchmark table: fev-bench (100 configs) MASE skill 0.3771 and SQL skill 0.4887, ahead of TimesFM-3 (0.3742, 0.4866) and Chronos-2 (0.3550, 0.4728). TIME (98 configs) MASE 0.6372, CRPS 0.5363 against TimesFM-3 0.6398, 0.5363. GIFT-Eval (97 configs) MASE 0.6806, CRPS 0.4688, behind TimesFM-3 (0.6668, 0.4557), ahead of Chronos-2 (0.6978, 0.4854).

title: Timer-M1 (full text, v1)
note: Fetched. Caveats the authors state: ranks are among the methods displayed, from fixed snapshots of public submissions, not an official zero-shot leaderboard placement; training-data exposure is not matched across models; the TIME margin over TimesFM-3 (0.40% MASE, under 0.01% CRPS in a matched rerun) is called competitive, not established superiority.

title: Timer-M1 (full text, v1)
note: Fetched. fev-bench by task type: on the 18 known-future-covariate tasks Timer-M1 is second to TimesFM-3 (MASE skill 0.4481 vs 0.4549; SQL skill 0.5363 vs 0.5458), ahead of Chronos-2 (0.4323, 0.5257). It leads on the 12 past-only tasks (MASE skill 0.4256 vs 0.3933). Learned gates lift known-future SQL skill to 0.5363 from 0.5002 with a fixed gate.
